title: Ukraine blew up Putin’s bridge using relay drones to bypass Starlink limits
gist: Ukraine collapsed a roadway arch of Russia's $3.5B Kerch Strait Bridge on Nov 15–16 using missiles (incl. homegrown Flamingo) guided via an airborne mesh-radio drone relay network adapted from Russian tactics, deliberately avoiding Starshield due to US speed restrictions; follow-up Neptune strikes hit the rail section, threatening Russia's Crimea supply lines.

insights.claim: Ukraine guided missiles and drones against the Kerch Strait Bridge using drones fitted with mesh radios as airborne relay nodes, letting operators more than 250 km away steer munitions around Russian air defenses.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Airborne mesh relay networks are an emerging alternative to satellite links for long-range strike command-and-control.
insights.locator: During the Ukrainian attacks on the Kerch Strait Bridge

insights.claim: The airborne drone mesh-network technique Ukraine used was adapted from a Russian battlefield innovation originally used for long-range strikes on Ukrainian cities.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Battlefield tech diffuses quickly between adversaries; counter-drone and mesh-radio demand will rise on both sides.
insights.locator: The Ukrainian operation adapted a Russian battlefield innovation

insights.claim: Ukrainian units deliberately avoided Starshield, the military version of SpaceX's Starlink, because US restrictions bar its use on drones or anything moving faster than 100 mph.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Political control over SpaceX's network is pushing militaries toward sovereign or non-satellite comms, a risk to Starshield's defense value proposition.
insights.quote: “Ukrainian units involved in the operation deliberately avoided using Starshield, the military version of Musk’s Starlink satellite network,”
insights.locator: Notably, Ukraine conducted the coordinated strike

insights.claim: Zelenskyy says the US-imposed Starshield speed restrictions remain in place and interfere with Ukrainian drone interceptors, while SpaceX denied the restrictions had returned.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Conflicting accounts underline the policy uncertainty around relying on a single commercial satellite provider in wartime.

insights.claim: The Kerch strike shows Ukraine's military and defense tech companies learning to fight without Starlink, mainly with Ukrainian-developed or adapted technologies such as the Flamingo cruise missile.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Ukraine's domestic defense-tech base is maturing; watch it as an exporter and as a reducer of dependence on US commercial systems.
insights.locator: However, the Ukrainian strikes on the Kerch Strait Bridge

insights.claim: Russian sources say several hundred Ukrainian drones overwhelmed air defenses before remote-controlled missile strikes, after weeks of preparatory strikes degrading Russian air defenses, radars and electronic warfare around the bridge.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Saturation drone swarms plus SEAD campaigns can defeat point defenses of high-value infrastructure.
insights.locator: Ukraine’s takedown of the bridge segment was preceded

insights.claim: The November 15 night attack coincided with the largest Ukrainian overnight drone attack on Russia since the start of the full-scale war, per Reuters.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Escalating Ukrainian long-range drone capacity raises risk to Russian infrastructure broadly.
insights.locator: Ukraine’s takedown of the bridge segment

insights.claim: After trains resumed on November 18, Ukraine struck the bridge's railway section with Ukrainian Navy Neptune cruise missiles, and Crimean officials temporarily suspended train traffic.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Ukraine is pursuing full interdiction of the bridge, not a one-off strike.
insights.locator: But Ukraine targeted the railway section yet again

insights.claim: The Institute for the Study of War assesses that destruction of the Kerch bridge will complicate Russia's ability to sustain its occupation and military basing in Crimea, while the alternative land route through occupied southern Ukraine is already under Ukrainian attack.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
entities: Institute for the Study of War
insights.so_what: Constraining Crimea supply weakens Russia's Black Sea position and could shift the war's negotiating leverage.
insights.locator: Meanwhile, the severe damage to the bridge’s arch

insights.claim: Debris from the collapsed arch may block large ship traffic through the Kerch Strait linking the Sea of Azov and Black Sea, further hampering Russia's sea resupply of Crimea.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: A blocked strait would disrupt Azov shipping, including commercial traffic, beyond military resupply.
insights.locator: Fallen debris from the bridge’s collapsed arch

insights.claim: Engineering experts told The New York Times that roadway repairs to the $3.5 billion bridge could take two years under normal conditions, longer if piers are damaged, with repairs exposed to further Ukrainian strikes.
insights.speaker: Jeremy Hsu
insights.so_what: Expect a prolonged loss of the bridge's road capacity, unlike prior 2022 and 2025 attacks that Russia repaired.
insights.locator: The Kerch Strait Bridge’s future prospects look much bleaker
